full_judgment:
2. The facts of the plaintiffs' case are that the opposite party Nos. 1-23 being plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 05 of 1994 initially for declaration of their raiyati right in the suit land but subsequently by amendment prayed for a declaration that the villagers have got customary right in the suit land impleading the petitioner and others as defendants alleging inter alia that the suit land measuring 2.70 acres of land in Plot No. 358 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 23 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 20 is a patito land for grazing the cattle. Urnacharan Aich and others were the owners of the suit land along with other lands in zamandari right. Haranath Roy and others were the owners in taluka interest under them. Under them, Kalu Bhuiyan was the owner and possessor in hawla interest. The CS Khatian was accordingly prepared in the names of all as mentioned above. Haranath Roy was the owner in 'Kha' and Udayatara Chowdhurani and others were the owners in 'Ka' group in taluka interest. Kalu Bhuiyan was the owner of the suit land under them in hawla interest. Crops did not grow in the suit land. Kalu Bhuiyan left behind the suit land along with other lands in favour of the general public of the village for their use some 100 years back. Even before that the general public used to graze their cattle in the suit land. At present, the people of the village graze cattle and the youngsters play in the suit land during dry season. During rainy season, water hyacinth and other weeds grow there and the people cut those things to feed their cattle. During the CS operation, the plots of Khatian No. 23 were recorded as being used by the general public except the suit plot in the remark's column of the khatian. The people of the village have no other land to graze their cattle. The people of the village have been possessing the suit land for more than hundred years as mentioned above by exerting their right, title and possession over the same. The possession as mentioned above was not obstructed by the defendants or anybody else. The title of the people has been perfected in the suit land by their uninterrupted peaceful possession therein. The defendant No. 1 has no title or possession in the suit land. He or his father or predecessor has/had no title in the suit land. The house is situated in the village of Ballai within the Police Station of Chandina. He in collusion with settlement officials got his name recorded in the SA Khatian along with others. He stays in Illiotgonj Bazar in connection with his business. The recording of his name in the SA Khatian is wrong, collusive and without any basis. During the recent settlement operation, the suit land has been recorded in the VP Khatian as being possessed by the general public. The defendant No. 1 raised objection against the said recording but the same was rejected. The defendant No. 1 thereafter filed Appeal No. 1213 of 1990 and in the said appeal, it was held on 22-9-1992 that the suit is a private property and the plaintiffs are in the forceful occupation of the same as mentioned in the remarks column of the khatian. The defendant No. 1 being emboldened by the said order is now claiming title over the suit land. For the reasons stated above, the plaintiffs have filed this under order 1 Rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure on behalf of the general public. 

 3. On the other hand, the petitioner being defendant No. 1 entered appearance in the suit and contested the same by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia the suit is barred by limitation and is not maintainable as per provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and also not maintainable in its present form. Haranath Roy had 6 annas 12 gondas 1 kana 1 kranti share in Khatian No. 23 as shown in group 'Kha' and the others had the remaining share and the khatian was correctly prepared and published in their names. In the said khatian out of eight plots, six were shown as paths and canals and those plots were used by general public. The land of the suit plot No. 358 is the gobam for grazing the cattle of the defendants. The defendant and his co-shares used the said land for grazing their cattle. This defendant purchased 1.50 acres of land of the suit plot for valuable consideration from other co-shares. The other co-shares after obtaining the consideration money amounting to Taka 2,000 executed a nadabi deed on 16-1-1990 in favour of the defendant. The defendant is the owner of 1.20 acres of land in the suit plot by way of inheritance and 1.50 acres of land by purchase in total 2.70 acres of land. It is to be mentioned here that Haranath Roy while owner in the possession of 1.20 acres of land died leaving behind four sons and by amicable settlement among the brothers Nibaran Chandra got, the suit land and he died leaving behind this defendant; Nethur Chandra Roy as his only heir. Nethur Chandra Roy got 1.20 acres of land by inheritance and 1.50 acres of land by purchase in total 2.70 acres of land and has been in possession of the same. The SA Khatian No. 20 in respect of the suit land has been correctly prepared and published in his name. This defendant has been regularly paying rents of the suit land. Neither the plaintiffs nor the predecessors had/have any interest or possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs never took any step to correct the khatian and had/have paid any rent of the suit land. The plaintiffs are terrorists and they have been trying to grab the suit land owned and possessed by this defendant on false claim. For the reasons stated above, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 16. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the evidence on record, I am of view that the essential conditions of acquiring a valid customary right have not been proved. But the unfortunately, the Trial Court by gratuitous finding held that the plaintiffs acquired customary right over the suit land and the Appellate Court without any independent assessment of evidence on record and legal position critically involved therein most illegally dittoed the judgment of the Trial Court. By lapse of time, the use of the suit land as pasturage (গোবাম) has lost its validity specially in the context of Bangladesh, a densely populated country in the world and due to the advance of science and technology, the cows are brought up scientifically in the abode of the villagers. The plaintiffs claimed that the suit land is a vested property of the Government. But the Government did not claim any title over the suit land. The contention of the defendant is that by way of inheritance and purchase, the defendant became owner of 2.70 acres of land and has been possessing the same and his name has been correctly prepared in the latest khatian and he has been regularly paying rent to the Government. The title of the defendant could not be assailed by the plaintiffs.
